name: Next.js App Router
rationale: Next.js App Router projects stay maintainable when route files compose feature modules and client boundaries remain narrow.

sources.label: Next.js App Router architecture
sources.note: Rules encode route composition, server/client component boundaries, and feature ownership patterns.

directories.purpose: Route segments, layouts, loading/error boundaries, and server composition.
Feature-owned UI, hooks, schemas, and client components.

fileRules.name: Thin route files
fileRules.rule: Next.js route files should compose feature modules and avoid owning business logic.
fileRules.trigger: A page/layout/route file is large, imports database clients, or defines substantial workflow logic.
fileRules.recommendation: Move workflow UI into src/features and server/data logic into src/server or src/db.
fileRules.goodExample: page.tsx imports and renders <BillingSettingsPage /> from src/features/billing.
fileRules.badExample: page.tsx contains form state, validation, database calls, and rendering in one file.

fileRules.name: Explicit client boundaries
fileRules.rule: Only mark components with 'use client' when browser state, effects, or event handlers are required.
fileRules.trigger: A broad route or layout file uses 'use client'.
fileRules.recommendation: Move interactive pieces into smaller client components and keep route composition server-rendered.
fileRules.goodExample: A small DatePicker component has 'use client'; page.tsx remains server-rendered.
fileRules.badExample: A full dashboard route has 'use client' to support one dropdown.

moduleBoundaries: Server components may fetch data, but client components must receive data through props or call explicit client-safe APIs.
Route handlers belong in app/api or server modules; reusable business logic belongs in src/server.
testingExpectations: Feature behavior should have component or integration tests outside route files.
Critical user flows should have at least one browser-level test.
agentInstructions: Do not place entire screens, forms, data access, and mutation handling in a single page.tsx file.
Split route composition, feature UI, validation, and server actions into focused files.
